title: Man dies after being Tasered by police
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit is probing the circumstances surrounding the death of a 42-year-old man who died in hospital after being Tasered last night by Peel Regional Police in Mississauga.

Brampton resident Sean Reilly was arrested at a residence in Mississauga on a charge of assault with a weapon and taken to 12 Division headquarters on Dixie Rd. just after 5 p.m., according to SIU spokesperson John Yoannou.
During a struggle in the cell area, a Taser was used to subdue him. Reilly went into medical distress and was taken to Trillium Health Centre, where he died this morning at around 4:45 a.m.
A post-mortem to determine the cause of death has not yet been scheduled.
The SIU has designated four subject officers and one witness officer as part of its investigation.

The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates cases of serious injuries (including allegations of sexual assault) and deaths involving the police. Under the Police Services Act, the Director of the SIU is mandated to consider whether a criminal offence has been committed by an officer in connection with the incident under investigation and, where warranted by the evidence, to cause a criminal charge or charges to be laid against the office.

The Taser is billed as an effective, less lethal weapon that can be used to subdue and gain control of violent subjects and reduce the possibility of serious injury to police officers and others involved.
It delivers a pulsating, 50,000-volt electrical current through the body and police say it can pierce clothing that is four-centimetres thick.
The shock, which lasts up to five seconds, locks muscles instantly and overrides the victim's central nervous system. But it isn't supposed to cause death.
